steps.name: QC, normalization, log2FC ranking
steps.context: Files: counts.csv (12000 x 3) and metadata.csv (2 x 2) under /eval-four-models-v2-without-no-replicates-1v1-s1-1/data/inputs/. Condition labels: treated vs control. Raw salmon gene-level counts; no length correction guaranteed, but for within-gene between-sample fold changes length correction is not required. With 1 sample per group, pydeseq2 cannot fit dispersion — use it (or manual median-of-ratios) ONLY for size factors, never for a statistical test.
steps.question: What are the per-gene fold changes between the treated and control liver sample after library-size normalization?
constraints: Do NOT run a statistical test or report p-values/p-adjusted — no replication makes them invalid
Report library sizes, counts sanity, and number of genes passing a minimal expression filter
Handle zero counts with a pseudocount (0.5) when taking log2 ratios
Order columns and sample ids from metadata.csv, not assumed names
steps.description: Load counts.csv (12,000 genes x 2 samples) and metadata.csv (2 rows, condition = treated/control). Verify sample-id agreement, report library sizes and gene detection. Compute median-of-ratios size factors for normalization, filter low-expression genes, and compute per-gene log2 fold change (treated vs control) on normalized counts with a pseudocount, plus log2CPM values. Output a full ranked gene table (gene, log2FC, normalized counts, log2CPM) and a summary of top up/down genes.
acceptance_criteria: counts and metadata load and align on sample ids (2 samples x 12000 genes)
size factors computed and reported per sample
filtered gene table (CPM threshold) with log2FC, log2CPM_treated, log2CPM_control written as TSV/CSV
top up- and down-regulated genes (|log2FC| >= 1) listed in step output

steps.name: Rank-based pathway enrichment (fgsea)
steps.context: Ranked list from T1S1. Reference: /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human/2026.07.10/wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt — HGNC gene symbols; if count gene ids are Ensembl/Entrez, map via /mnt/refs/managed/uniprot-idmapping-human/current/HUMAN_9606_idmapping_selected.tab.gz (positional, no header; col3 = Entrez, col19 = Ensembl). Report if the reference is absent; the run then ends with the ranked gene list alone.
steps.question: Which human WikiPathways pathways show coherent log2FC shifts toward the treated sample?
constraints: Rank metric = log2FC only (no test statistic exists)
Use min/max pathway sizes (e.g. 10/500) and report the number of genes mapping into the gene sets
If the WikiPathways reference is unavailable, report that enrichment was skipped and output the ranked list only
steps.description: Run fgsea on the log2FC-ranked gene list from T1S1 against the WikiPathways Homo sapiens gene sets to identify pathways with coherent shift toward the treated or control sample. Because there is one sample per condition, NES direction is interpretable but significance is not — present NES values as descriptive enrichment, explicitly labeled as such.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea runs on the log2FC ranking with WikiPathways human gene sets
report shows top enriched pathways per direction with NES and size, stated as untested rankings (no p-value interpretation)
gene ID space (counts gene ids vs HGNC symbols) reconciled explicitly; unmapped fraction reported

steps.name: Report: fold-change ranking with replication caveat
steps.context: Inputs: ranked gene table (T1S1) and fgsea table (T1S2). Audience needs effect sizes, not significance claims.
steps.question: Which genes shift most between treated and control, and in which pathways — with correct statistical caveats?
constraints: Never describe log2FC lists as 'significantly differentially expressed'
State that salmon counts may lack length correction and why that does not affect within-gene fold changes
steps.description: Assemble the final deliverable: ranked gene table (top up/down by log2FC), descriptive pathway enrichment table (fgsea NES, no p-value claims), QC metrics, and a prominent caveat that with 1 treated vs 1 control sample these are untested fold changes for hypothesis generation, not differential expression calls.
acceptance_criteria: table with genes ranked by |log2FC| including normalized expression values
heatmap/summary of top 50 |log2FC| genes across the two samples
explicit caveat section: no biological replication, no variance estimate, no p-values; findings are hypothesis-generating only
pathway table from T1S2 integrated with directional interpretation (treated-up / control-up)

plan.title: 1v1 treated vs control liver: fold-change ranking + rank-based pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The design is one treated vs one control liver sample (12,000 genes, salmon-derived raw counts, no biological replication). With n=1 per group no dispersion can be estimated and no statistical test for differential expression is valid — any p-value would be meaningless. The plan therefore produces an honest exploratory analysis: (1) QC and library-size normalization (median-of-ratios size factors), (2) an effect-size-ranked gene list (log2 fold change with a pseudocount, plus a minimal expression filter), (3) rank-based pathway enrichment (fgsea on the log2FC ranking) against human WikiPathways to give biological context, and (4) a report that states clearly that results are unscored fold changes, not tested differential expression. No step claims statistical significance.

No step claims statistical significance.
